context:
Goal: a message wakes an idle session on any machine.
Problem (rule): the only portable route is a waiting process, and rule outcomes-mechanize-rules forbids long-lived processes and timers.
Based on (read): mail is read only at turn start (hooks/mail.py); the cloud routes (PR alerts, a webhook) do not exist in local Claude Code; your 14:14 CST answer: "keep mail only ... the doorbell was supposed to be via a whole other route that's translatable anywhere".
Departs from: main, where an idle session never wakes — adds one waiting process per idle session, or a cloud-only bell.
home: step mailbox-doorbell (a message wakes an idle session anywhere)

lastAnswer.note: Owner 14:17 CST in retrospective chat: "I'm okay with A for Q1" (R57, plan 79eb441). Note: ruling 3.15 (Nov 11, 13:22 CST) already allows a timer that costs less than it saves, so no exception is needed.

options.gain: Portable: git and Claude Code only.
options.how: A background mail-wait exits when mail lands, which wakes the session the same way everywhere; the rule gains a stated exception.
options.label: A mail-wait process (Recommended)
options.lose: One sleeping process per idle session, plus a cheap git read every so often (interval unmeasured).

options.label: Cloud-only doorbell for now
